options.title: Taxi to Seoul Station with the bags
options.name: Seoul Station
options.about: The terminus for the KTX to Busan, a landmark since 1925 — the old red-brick station stands beside the modern glass one.
tips: Lockers, cafés and a snack floor inside for the train.
KTX platforms are on the ground level — check the board for your train number.

options.title: Metro Line 2 → Line 4 with the bags
options.name: 서울역
options.about: Konkuk Univ. → Line 2 to Dongdaemun History & Culture Park → Line 4 to Seoul Station: two trains, one easy change, elevators at both ends.
options.cool: Cheap and traffic-proof — worth it if the bags roll well.
tips: Leave by 08:45 for the 10:00 train — buffer for the ticket gates.
Seoul Station exit 1 / 2 lead straight to the KTX hall.
options.fixed: Konkuk Univ. → Line 2 to Dongdaemun History & Culture Park → Line 4 to Seoul Station, ≈35 min with elevators at both ends. Leave by 08:45.

options.title: KTX Seoul → Busan
options.name: Busan Station
options.about: Korea's high-speed train (up to 305 km/h) covers the 417 km to Busan in under three hours, past Daejeon, Daegu and the Gyeongju hills.
tips: Book at letskorail.com or the Korail Talk app as soon as sales open.
Snack cart and vending in car 4; Wi-Fi on board.
options.fixed: KTX from Seoul Station, ≈2 h 40 min, ≈₩60k per person. Sit on the right (D seats) for the Nakdong river near Busan.

options.title: SRT from Suseo → Busan (back-up)
options.name: 수서역
options.about: The second high-speed line leaves from Suseo in the south-east: slightly cheaper and faster, handy if the KTX sells out — but Suseo is 35 min by metro from Konkuk.
options.cool: A quieter station and ₩8k cheaper per seat.
tips: Book at srtrain.co.kr (foreign cards work).
Line 3 or the Bundang line to Suseo; allow an hour door to door.
options.fixed: From Konkuk: Line 7 → Line 3 (or the Suin-Bundang line) to Suseo ≈35–40 min, or a taxi ≈30 min (≈₩20k). Be there 20 min before departure.

items.title: Lunch at Busan Station
items.fixed: Both are a 3–5 min walk from the station's main exit. Leave the bags in a station locker (≈₩3–4k) or roll them along — it's flat.

options.title: Choryang Milmyeon
options.name: 초량밀면
options.about: Busan's own noodle: chewy wheat noodles in an icy beef broth with a dab of spicy sauce, born in the refugee kitchens of the 1950s. This is the branch Busan people send you to.
options.cool: Milmyeon exists only in Busan — start the visit with it.
tips: 'Mul' (broth) or 'bibim' (dry, spicy) — get one of each and swap.
Add a plate of mandu (₩6k).

options.title: Bonjeon Dwaeji Gukbap
options.name: 본전돼지국밥
options.about: Right across from the station: the Michelin Bib Gourmand dwaeji-gukbap that Busanites queue for — a milky, clean pork broth over rice, seasoned with salted shrimp and chives.
options.cool: Busan's comfort food at its most famous address.
tips: One bowl each (≈₩10k); add a side of suyuk (boiled pork) to share if hungry.
Season with saeu-jeot (salted shrimp) and a spoon of the chives.

items.title: Check in at Hotel Aqua Palace, rest
items.metro: Metro alternative: Line 1 Busan Station → Seomyeon, Line 2 → Gwangan (exit 3), ≈40 min.
tips: Ask for a bridge-view room.
The hotel bathhouse is naked and gender-separated; swimsuits for the pool.

options.title: Millak Waterside Park
options.name: Millak Waterside Park
options.about: Wide stone steps down to the water at the eastern end of Gwangalli — the best free seat for the 7.4 km Gwangan Bridge at dusk.
options.cool: Beer and snacks from the convenience store behind you.
tips: Sit on the steps facing the bridge; it lights up at dusk.
The drone show is Saturdays only — you get the bridge lights anyway.

options.title: Igidae coastal walk
options.name: Igidae Coastal Walk
options.about: A boardwalk and cliff path on the headland south of Gwangalli, looking straight back at the bridge and the Haeundae skyline across the bay.
options.cool: The best angle on the bridge at sunset, with the sea below you.
tips: Start at the Dongsaengmal viewpoint (taxi drop-off) and walk 20 min north for the views.
Some steps — wear trainers.

options.title: Millak Fisherman's Market — raw fish upstairs
options.type: Seafood · raw fish (hoe) with a view
options.price: ≈₩30–35k per person, food only · ₩5k pp table charge
options.name: 민락어민활어직판장
options.about: Pick a live fish from a vendor downstairs, carry it upstairs, and eat it as sashimi facing the lit-up Gwangan Bridge — the Busan dinner.
options.cool: Bridge view, plastic chairs, the freshest fish in the city.
options.booking: None. Set a budget with the vendor first (≈₩50–60k of fish for two) and confirm the ₩5k-per-person seating charge upstairs.
tips: Budget tip: say '5만원어치' (₩50k worth) and stick to it — flounder and sea bream are the value picks.
Finish with maeuntang (spicy fish stew) made from the bones, ≈₩10k.

options.title: Gwangan Jeil Dwaeji Gukbap
options.name: 광안제일돼지국밥
options.about: The neighbourhood gukbap house two blocks behind the beach — a clean, rich pork broth and a menu you can read in ten seconds.
options.cool: Open late, cheap, and five minutes from the hotel.
tips: Add suyuk-baekban (boiled pork with rice) if one of you wants something less soupy.

options.title: Night yacht on Suyeongman Bay
options.name: 수영만요트경기장
options.about: A 50-minute sail under the lit Gwangan Bridge and along the Marine City towers from the 1988 Olympic yachting centre — the bay at night from the water.
tips: Book on Trazy or Klook; pick the 20:00 sailing.
Cold on deck — bring the layer.
Taxi back to the hotel ≈8 min, ≈₩6k.
options.cool: Under the lit bridge from the water; Marine City towers overhead.
options.booking: Book on Trazy or Klook; weekday sailings hourly 18:00–21:00.

options.title: Gwangalli beach night walk & bridge lights
options.name: 광안리해수욕장
options.about: The 1.4 km beach promenade after dark with the whole Gwangan Bridge lit in changing colours, then a can of beer on the sand.
options.cool: Zero cost, five minutes from the hotel; the bridge light show runs nightly.
tips: Walk east to Millak and back.
'Beer street' is one block behind the beach for a nightcap.

options.title: Haeundae Blueline beach train at night
options.name: 해운대 블루라인파크 해변열차
options.about: The slow beach train along the lit coast from Mipo to Cheongsapo and back — the same line as tomorrow's capsule, from the other carriage.
options.cool: Harbour lights and the dark sea; far fewer people than by day.
options.booking: Walk-up; last trains ≈21:00 in November — check the day's timetable.
tips: Taxi ≈15 min from Gwangalli.
If you ride tonight, tomorrow's capsule still feels different — it's the view down.

items.title: Along the Blueline coast
items.fixed: Leave the hotel at 09:30 — taxi ≈15 min (≈₩12k) to Mipo station at the east end of Haeundae beach. Check in 15 min before your slot.

options.title: Sky Capsule, Mipo → Cheongsapo
options.name: Blueline Park, Mipo Station
options.about: Private four-seat pods gliding 7–10 m above the shoreline on the old railway line from Mipo to Cheongsapo — Busan's most photographed ride.
tips: Bookings open Tue 6 Oct 09:00 KST = 02:00 Munich — the 10:00 slot sells out fast.
Sit on the sea side; the colourful pods over the water are the photo.

options.title: Blueline Beach Train instead (cheaper, no booking)
options.name: 해운대 블루라인파크 해변열차
options.about: The slow red beach train runs the same clifftop track as the capsules, with big windows facing the sea; hop on at Mipo and off at Cheongsapo.
options.cool: Walk-up tickets, same views, a third of the price.
tips: Sit on the sea side (left going north).
If capsules are sold out, this is the plan — no booking needed.

items.title: Cheongsapo
items.fixed: The capsule drops you at Cheongsapo station; the skywalk is a 10-min walk east along the old tracks (follow the boardwalk).

options.title: Cheongsapo Daritdol Skywalk
options.name: Cheongsapo Daritdol Skywalk
options.about: A 72 m glass-bottomed walkway jutting out over the rocks beside a fishing village with twin red-and-white lighthouses.
tips: Shoe covers are provided for the glass section.
The lighthouses are 5 min back toward the harbour.

options.title: Cheongsapo harbour & twin lighthouses
options.name: 청사포 등대
options.about: A tiny fishing harbour with a red and a white lighthouse at the end of the breakwaters, drying seaweed on the quay and cafés tucked above the rocks.
options.cool: Walk out to the red lighthouse — the view back to the village is pure Busan.
tips: Grilled clams restaurants here are the lunch option next.
Watch the slippery breakwater steps after rain.

options.title: Suminine — grilled shellfish, smallest set
options.name: 수민이네 청사포
options.about: The harbour's grilled-shellfish house: a tray of clams, scallops and abalone over charcoal at your table, with cheese-baked scallops and a kimchi-fried-rice finish.
options.cool: Sea view from the second floor; the whole harbour smells of it.
tips: Budget tip: order the smallest set (≈₩60–70k for two) and skip the abalone upgrade.
Ask for the kimchi bokkeumbap at the end — cooked in the shell juices.

options.title: Geumsu Bokguk — regular soup
options.name: 금수복국 해운대본점
options.about: Busan's most famous bokguk (pufferfish soup) since 1970: a clear, restorative broth with bean sprouts and water parsley — the city's classic hangover cure.
options.cool: Open 24 hours; the safest, cleanest way to try fugu.
tips: Budget tip: the regular 'eun-bok' soup (≈₩16k) — the premium fish versions run to ₩40k+.
Taxi ≈12 min from Cheongsapo, on the way to the temple.

options.title: Haedong Yonggungsa Temple
options.name: Haedong Yonggungsa Temple
options.about: A Buddhist temple from 1376 built on the rocks above the waves in Gijang — one of very few Korean temples on the coast rather than in the mountains.
tips: 108 steps down to the temple; rub the golden pigs for luck.
Weekends are packed — a Tuesday is ideal.

options.title: Songjeong Beach & Jukdo Park
options.name: 송정해수욕장
options.about: Busan's laid-back surf beach, two stops up the coast: a wide crescent of sand, a wooden boardwalk, surf cafés and the little pine-covered Jukdo islet at the end.
options.cool: Empty sand in November and the best flat-white on the coast.
tips: Taxi from Cheongsapo ≈8 min.
Jukdo Park pavilion at the north end is the sunset spot.

options.title: BUSAN X the SKY
options.name: BUSAN X the SKY
options.about: The observatory on floors 98–100 of the LCT tower at the east end of Haeundae beach — the beach, Gwangan Bridge and the coast you rode this morning, from 384 m.
options.cool: Starbucks on the 99th floor is the highest in the world.
options.booking: Walk-up or online; sunset slots are busiest.
tips: Be up by 16:45 for the 17:25 sunset.
Taxi ≈20 min from the temple.

options.title: Dongbaekseom island walk
options.name: Dongbaekseom Island
options.about: The pine-covered headland at the west end of Haeundae: a flat boardwalk loop around the island with the APEC House, a mermaid statue and the bridge across the bay.
options.cool: Sunset from the western rocks, then the beach lights on the walk back.
tips: Start from the Westin/Chosun side and walk anticlockwise.
Taxi ≈25 min from the temple.

options.title: Sangguginae, Haeundae Market
options.type: Busan street food · tteokbokki, fish cake, gimbap
options.name: 상국이네 해운대시장
options.about: The most famous stall in Haeundae Market: tteokbokki, eomuk skewers in broth, fried gimbap and sundae eaten standing at the counter.
options.cool: Loud, hot, ₩10k for two — Busan snack culture in one stop.
tips: Add the grilled eel restaurants next door if you're still hungry (≈₩20k).
Taxi home ≈15 min.

options.title: Geumsu Bokguk (24 h)
options.name: 금수복국 해운대본점
options.about: If you had clams at lunch, dinner is the bokguk you skipped — a clear pufferfish broth that's as good at night as it is in the morning.
options.cool: Open 24 h, 5 min from the beach.
tips: Regular soup ≈₩16k; skip the premium fish upgrades.

options.title: The Bay 101 — Marine City night view
options.name: 더베이101
options.about: A yacht-club deck opposite the Marine City towers, which mirror in the still water of the marina after dark — Busan's postcard night shot.
options.cool: Fish and chips and a beer on the deck; the reflections are the photo.
tips: Taxi ≈7 min from Haeundae Market.
Then a taxi home ≈15 min.

options.title: Haeundae beach lights & Gunam-ro
options.name: 해운대해수욕장
options.about: The beach after dark with the LCT tower lit above it, then the busy Gunam-ro pedestrian street of buskers and bars.
options.cool: Street performers most evenings around the Gunam-ro fountain.
tips: Five minutes from the market.
Taxi home ≈15 min.

options.title: Busan Cinema Center LED roof
options.name: 영화의전당
options.about: The world's longest cantilever roof, a 163 m wing of LEDs that plays light sequences over the plaza where the Busan film festival opens.
options.cool: Quiet, odd and beautiful; ten minutes from Spa Land.
tips: Taxi ≈12 min from Haeundae.
Taxi home to Gwangalli ≈10 min.

items.title: Old Busan morning
items.metro: Leave 09:00 — taxi across town is simplest (≈35 min); the metro needs Line 2 → Line 1 → bus 2-2 up the hill.

options.title: Gamcheon Culture Village
options.name: Gamcheon Culture Village
options.about: A 1950s refugee settlement of pastel houses stacked up the hillside, turned into an open-air art village in 2009.
tips: Buy the stamp map at the info centre and collect stamps for a free postcard.
The Little Prince viewpoint has a queue — go there first.
Steep stairs: good shoes.

options.title: Bosu-dong Book Alley & Bupyeong Kkangtong Market
options.name: 보수동 책방골목
options.about: A lane of 50 second-hand bookshops stacked to the ceilings, then the covered Kkangtong ("tin can") market next door — Busan as it was before the murals.
options.cool: Real old Busan with zero tour buses, and it's on the way to Jagalchi.
tips: Korean picture books make lovely cheap gifts.
Kkangtong Market has a night-market street from 18:00 — different vibe.

options.title: Jagalchi Market 2F grilled fish + BIFF hotteok
options.type: Seafood · grilled fish set, then a seed pancake
options.name: Jagalchi Market
options.about: Korea's largest fish market: on the second floor, restaurants grill mackerel, hairtail and eel over charcoal and serve them as a set with rice and soup. Then walk 5 min to BIFF Square for ssiat-hotteok.
options.cool: Grilled-fish set (₩12–15k) beats buying live fish for value; the seed-stuffed hotteok (₩2k) is Busan's iconic snack.
tips: Budget tip: order the 'saengseon-gui jeongsik' (grilled fish set) rather than by-weight fish.
Nampo station exit 2 for BIFF Square.

options.title: Halmae Gaya Milmyeon
options.name: 할매가야밀면
options.about: A Nampo-dong milmyeon house from the 1970s, two minutes from BIFF Square — plain bowls, icy broth, no fuss.
options.cool: The Nampo locals' lunch; ₩8k bowls.
tips: Order 'mul-milmyeon' and a plate of mandu.
Then hotteok at BIFF Square anyway.

options.title: Huinnyeoul Culture Village
options.name: Huinnyeoul Culture Village
options.about: White-washed houses on a cliff above the sea on Yeongdo island, with a coastal path, a tunnel through the rock and cafés hanging over the water.
options.cool: Stay for the 17:24 sunset over the anchored ships.
tips: Taxi ≈15 min across the Yeongdo bridge.
Featured in the film 'The Attorney' — hence the murals.

options.title: Songdo Marine Cable Car
options.type: Cable car · 1.6 km over the sea
options.name: Songdo Marine Cable Car
options.about: Cabins crossing 1.6 km of open water from Songdo beach to Amnam Park's cliffs, with a coastal skywalk and a cliff trail on the far side.
options.cool: Crystal-floor cabins look straight down at the sea.
tips: Taxi ≈10 min from Jagalchi.
Walk Amnam Park's cliff path for 30 min before riding back.

options.title: Taejongdae
options.name: Taejongdae
options.about: The wooded southern tip of Yeongdo: 100 m sea cliffs, a lighthouse and an observatory looking out to where Tsushima appears on clear days.
options.cool: The Danubi road train loops the park so you don't have to climb.
tips: Taxi ≈25 min from Jagalchi.
Weekday afternoons are quiet.

options.title: Spa Land Centum City
options.name: Spa Land Centum City
options.about: Korea's most luxurious jjimjilbang, inside the world's largest department store: 22 hot-spring baths from two natural sources, 13 themed saunas, an open-air foot spa and a relaxation lounge.
options.cool: The Roman bath and the Finnish sauna; couples meet in the mixed sauna zone in the spa uniform.
tips: Taxi ≈25 min from Yeongdo, ≈10 min from the hotel afterwards.
Baths are naked and gender-separated; the themed saunas are mixed.

options.title: Hotel spa & beach walk
options.name: Hotel Aqua Palace
options.about: Back to Gwangalli for the hotel's own bathhouse, then a slow walk along the beach under the bridge lights.
options.cool: No travel, bridge view, bed nearby.
tips: Gwangalli has a 'beer street' one block behind the beach for a nightcap.

options.title: Gwangan Jeil Dwaeji Gukbap
options.name: 광안제일돼지국밥
options.about: The neighbourhood gukbap house behind Gwangalli beach — open late and five minutes from the hotel.
options.cool: A hot bowl at 21:00 after the spa.
tips: Add suyuk-baekban if you want something less soupy.

options.title: 1953 Hyeongje Dwaeji Gukbap, Seomyeon
options.name: 1953 형제돼지국밥
options.about: On Seomyeon's 'gukbap alley': a 70-year-old kitchen serving a milkier, richer style of the soup, open around the clock.
options.cool: The oldest name on the alley; Seomyeon's neon streets outside.
tips: Line 2 from Centum City to Seomyeon ≈20 min; taxi home from Seomyeon ≈20 min.

options.title: Samjin Eomuk at Busan Station
options.name: 삼진어묵 부산역점
options.about: Busan's oldest fish-cake maker (1953) runs a bakery-style shop inside the station: trays of warm fish cakes stuffed with cheese, shrimp or peppers — the train picnic.
tips: Buy 5–6 pieces and a coffee; eat them on the train.
Card accepted.

options.title: Station food court: kimbap, coffee & pastries
options.name: 부산역 푸드코트
options.about: The second floor of Busan Station has a food court and bakeries — kimbap rolls, egg sandwiches, coffee — right next to the KTX gates.
options.cool: Fast, cheap and you can eat it on the train.
tips: Buy two coffees — KTX has no café car.
Convenience store at platform level if you're late.

items.title: Train back to Seoul
items.fixed: KTX from Busan Station, ≈2 h 40 min. Left side (A seats) for the river views this time.

options.title: KTX Busan → Seoul
options.name: Seoul Station
options.about: The same route in reverse — back in Seoul by early afternoon.
tips: Platforms are upstairs at Busan Station; check the board.

options.title: SRT Busan → Suseo (back-up)
options.name: 부산역 SRT
options.about: If the KTX is full, the SRT reaches Suseo in south-east Seoul in 2 h 20; from Suseo the glue hotel is ≈40 min by metro (Line 3 → Jongno 3-ga) or a 35-min taxi.
options.cool: Slightly cheaper and often has seats when KTX is sold out.
tips: Book at srtrain.co.kr.
From Suseo take Line 3 to Anguk and a 10-min taxi to the hotel.

items.title: Check in at glue hotel
items.fixed: From Seoul Station a taxi (≈20–25 min, ≈₩13–15k) is recommended because of the bags. Metro alternative: Line 4 to Hyehwa + an 11-min walk.
tips: Rooftop faces Naksan; the lounge has live sets ≈20:00–22:00.

options.title: Naksan fortress wall at sunset
options.name: Naksan Fortress Wall Trail
options.about: A section of the 600-year-old Seoul City Wall climbs Naksan hill behind the hotel — murals on the way up, the whole skyline from the top.
tips: Walk up through Ihwa Mural Village.
Naksan Park terrace has the best downtown skyline view.

options.title: Ihwa Mural Village lanes
options.name: 이화벽화마을
options.about: The steep lanes below the fortress wall: stair murals, tiny cafés, rooftop views over Dongdaemun — the same sunset from a lower, cosier angle.
options.cool: Flowers-on-stairs photo spot and a rooftop café for the sunset.
options.hours: Always open (quiet after 20:00, residents live here)
tips: Keep voices down — it's a residential hill.
Café 개뿔 rooftop faces the sunset.

options.title: Sunhui-ne Bindaetteok
options.name: 순희네빈대떡
options.about: The market's most famous bindaetteok stall: mung beans ground in front of you and fried in a pool of oil, eaten on a plastic stool with makgeolli.
options.cool: Netflix-famous, and still ₩5k a pancake.
tips: Two pancakes and a bowl of makgeolli (≈₩5k) between you.
Mostly cash.

options.title: Buchon Yukhoe
options.name: 부촌육회
options.about: On Gwangjang's yukhoe alley: hand-cut raw beef with pear, sesame oil and a raw egg yolk — Michelin Bib Gourmand and the best-known of the alley's shops.
options.cool: Order the yukhoe-bibimbap for something more filling.
tips: Budget tip: one plate of yukhoe (≈₩20k) shared plus a bibimbap keeps it under ₩20k each.
Then a bindaetteok for dessert anyway.

options.title: Live music in the hotel lounge
options.name: glue hotel
options.about: The hotel lounge hosts small live sets most evenings ≈20:00–22:00 — a soft landing after the market.
options.cool: Zero commute.
options.booking: Ask the front desk for tonight's set.

options.title: DDP at night
options.name: Dongdaemun Design Plaza
options.about: Zaha Hadid's silver spaceship of a building, lit at night, with the LED rose garden on the lawn and Dongdaemun's 24-hour fashion malls around it.
options.cool: Ten minutes' walk from Gwangjang Market; the roses glow after dark.
tips: Taxi back to the hotel ≈7 min.

options.title: A small Daehangno play
options.name: 대학로 소극장
options.about: Daehangno has over a hundred small theatres around Hyehwa station; comedies and musicals with easy plots work even without Korean.
options.cool: Tickets at the booth on the Marronnier Park square; same-day discounts are common.
options.booking: Same-day at the ticket booth, or Interpark for English listings.
tips: Five minutes' walk from the hotel.
Pick a non-verbal show (Nanta-style) if you want zero language barrier.

items.title: Changdeokgung morning
items.metro: Leave the hotel at 09:35 — ≈25 min on foot along Changgyeonggung-ro, or a 5-min taxi.

options.title: Changdeokgung & Secret Garden tour
options.name: Changdeokgung Secret Garden
options.about: A UNESCO-listed palace laid into the hillside, with the 32-hectare Huwon (Secret Garden) of pavilions and lotus ponds behind it — the loveliest place in Seoul in autumn.
tips: Garden tickets are released 6 days ahead at royal.khs.go.kr — 50 online, 50 on-site per slot.
Peak colour in the garden: late Oct – early Nov.

options.title: Changdeokgung palace only + Bukchon viewpoint
options.name: 창덕궁
options.about: Skip the timed garden tour and wander the main palace at your own pace — the most beautiful of the five — then climb to the Bukchon 6th view for the hanok-roofs-and-palace photo.
options.cool: No slot to chase; the Injeongjeon hall and Nakseonjae are stunning on their own.
tips: Still free with the 4-palace pass if you bought one.
Bukchon-ro 11-gil for the classic view, 10 min walk.

options.title: Changgyeonggung glasshouse
options.name: Changgyeonggung Palace
options.about: The quieter palace next door: a 1909 Victorian glasshouse (Korea's first), the Chundangji pond you saw lit up on Thursday, and almost no crowds.
tips: The glasshouse is at the far north end past the pond.
Exit through Honghwamun onto Changgyeonggung-ro.
options.fixed: Use the Hamyangmun connecting gate on the east side of Changdeokgung — the two palaces join directly. Changgyeonggung ticket ₩1,000 at the gate.

options.title: Ikseon-dong hanok alleys
options.name: 익선동
options.about: A maze of 1920s hanok turned into tiny cafés, tea rooms and shops a few minutes south of the palace — Seoul's prettiest alleys for an unhurried hour.
options.cool: Low roofs, lanterns and good coffee all within 200 m.
tips: Lunch options are right here (Changhwadang is in Ikseon).
Narrow lanes: go before 12:00 to beat the weekend crowd.

options.title: Changhwadang Ikseon
options.type: Korean · dumplings & tteokbokki in a hanok
options.name: 창화당 익선점
options.about: In the 1920s hanok lanes of Ikseon-dong: crisp pan-fried dumplings, cheese tteokbokki and cold noodles, at long wooden tables under a glass roof.
options.cool: The lanes themselves — go before 12:30 or queue.
options.booking: None; waitlist app at the door.
tips: Two dumpling plates + one tteokbokki between you ≈₩28k total.
Dessert at Cheongsudang's garden café next door.

options.title: Woo Lae Oak — cold noodles only
options.name: Woo Lae Oak
options.about: If you skipped it on Thursday: Seoul's legendary 1946 naengmyeon house, 12 minutes' walk south.
options.cool: The definitive Pyongyang cold noodles.
tips: Budget tip: naengmyeon only (≈₩17k); the bulgogi is ₩50k+.

options.title: Rest at the hotel
options.name: glue hotel
options.about: Pack, nap, rooftop. The last big day deserves a pause.
options.cool: Zero commute.

options.title: Last gifts in Insadong
options.name: Insadong
options.about: Ten minutes' walk: hanji paper, ceramics, tea and the Ssamziegil craft arcade for the final presents.
options.cool: Tax refund at the counter over ₩15k.
tips: Kyung-in Museum of Fine Art has a hanok tea garden for a break.

options.title: Jongmyo Shrine — English guided tour
options.name: Jongmyo Shrine
options.about: The Confucian shrine to the Joseon kings — a 100 m-long hall of dark wood and stone, UNESCO-listed, and the quietest world-heritage site in downtown Seoul.
options.hours: Weekdays by guided tour only · English tours 10:00 / 12:00 / 14:00 / 16:00
tips: Be at the ticket gate by 15:50 — the 16:00 English tour is the last.
Saturdays are free-roaming; weekdays guided only.

options.title: Cheonggyecheon stream walk
options.name: 청계천
options.about: Drop below street level and follow the restored stream west from Gwangjang towards Gwangtonggyo: stepping stones, bridges, and lanterns switching on as the light goes.
options.cool: A calm 2 km of water through the middle of the city — perfect before a farewell dinner.
tips: Walk west: the lanterns are best between Gwanggyo and Cheonggye Plaza.
Jongsamyook BBQ is a 10-min walk back east.

options.title: Jongsamyook
options.price: ≈₩25–35k per person, food only (≈150–200 g pp)
options.name: 종삼육
options.about: A polished grill house by Jongno 3-ga where the staff cook thick-cut aged pork and beef over charcoal for you, with kimchi stew to finish.
options.cool: Staff-grilled, so you can just hold hands and eat.
options.booking: Reserve a 18:30 table via Catch Table or Naver a few days ahead.
tips: Budget tip: 300–400 g between two plus one stew stays under ₩35k each.
Drinks extra: soju ≈₩5k, beer ≈₩5k.

options.title: Hando Samgyeopsal
options.price: ≈₩18–25k per person, food only (sets ≈₩13–14k per portion)
options.name: 한도삼겹살
options.about: The old-school neighbourhood grill: thick pork belly on a slanted iron plate with kimchi and bean sprouts frying in the fat, and a bowl of doenjang stew.
options.cool: Cheap, loud and exactly what a last night in Seoul should taste like.
tips: Two portions (≈₩27k) + rice + stew is plenty for two.
Order 'mokssal' (neck) too if you want variety.

options.title: Namsan night view from Baekbeom Square
options.name: 백범광장
options.about: The lawn terraces on Namsan's north slope with the tower lit above you and the whole downtown glittering below — where you started eleven nights ago.
options.cool: Bring a convenience-store drink; the fortress wall is lit along the path.
tips: Taxi ≈12 min from Jongno 3-ga (≈₩8k).
Taxi back to the hotel ≈15 min.

options.title: Gwanghwamun Square by night
options.name: 광화문광장
options.about: The great axis of Seoul lit at night: King Sejong and Admiral Yi, the floodlit Gwanghwamun gate, and the fountains along the square.
options.cool: Fifteen minutes' walk from the barbecue; benches and the media wall.
tips: Walk down Cheonggyecheon on the way back.
Taxi home ≈10 min.

options.title: Rooftop at glue hotel
options.name: glue hotel
options.about: Naksan's wall lit above the hotel, the last bags half-packed, and nowhere else to be.
options.cool: Zero commute; the lounge set is on until 22:00.

options.title: Airport bus 6011 from the Changgyeonggung stop
options.name: 인천국제공항
options.about: Incheon International Airport — the way home. Hold hands in the queue.
tips: Check your terminal — T1 or T2.
Tax-refund counters are after security; keep the receipts handy.
options.fixed: Airport bus 6011 from the Changgyeonggung stop (≈10 min walk from the hotel): ≈70–80 min, ≈₩17–18k per person. Taxi: ≈60–75 min, ≈₩65–80k per car.

options.title: Taxi to Incheon
options.name: 인천국제공항
options.about: Door to door with the bags, ≈60–75 min outside rush hour via the airport expressway; Kakao T shows the fixed estimate before you book.
options.cool: Zero hassle for two people with luggage.
tips: Say which terminal — Terminal 1 for most airlines, 2 for KAL/Delta/Air France/KLM.
Book via Kakao T to avoid negotiating.
options.fixed: Taxi from the hotel door: ≈60–75 min outside rush hour, ≈₩65–80k per car plus the ₩6,600 expressway toll. Leave ≥3.5 h before the flight.

options.title: AREX express from Seoul Station
options.name: 서울역 공항철도
options.about: Taxi 15 min to Seoul Station, then the non-stop AREX Express to Incheon T1 in 43 min (T2 51 min); some airlines allow check-in at Seoul Station.
options.cool: Traffic-proof and you can drop bags early at the station check-in counters.
tips: Check if your airline offers city check-in at Seoul Station (KAL, Asiana, Jeju Air).
Buy express tickets at the machines — the all-stop train takes 20 min longer.
options.fixed: Taxi ≈15 min to Seoul Station (≈₩10k), then the AREX Express: 43 min to Terminal 1, 51 min to Terminal 2. Leave ≥3.5 h before the flight.
